correctness.rationale: For crown K_{n,n} minus one perfect matching, n>=5 and unit-rate unnormalized Laplacian, the row-kernel spectrum has eigenvalues 0, 2(n-1), n-2, n. There are exactly three vertex-pair orbits. Same-part W1/d equals alpha=exp(-(n-2)t); matched-nonedge W1/d equals alpha+(n-4)c/3; an adjacent pair attains alpha+(n-4)c with c=(alpha-exp(-2(n-1)t))/n>0 by a unit-cost bijective matching of signed row masses. The corresponding Kantorovich potentials give the lower bounds. Thus the full norm is [2(n-2)alpha-(n-4)exp(-2(n-1)t)]/n, adjacent pairs uniquely maximize for t>0, and -d(log C)/dt is strictly increasing 2 to n-2; n=4 is explicitly excluded from strict acceleration. Concavity of log C with value 0 at time zero establishes strict submultiplicativity. Independent matrix-exp/LP computation checked all pair ratios for n=5,6,8 and t=0.03,0.2,0.7, with zero discrepancies beyond numerical tolerance. n>=5 and arbitrary t are covered symbolically, not inferred from finite sampling.
